text: Applying flip-and-add-one to the 8-bit pattern 10000000 gives back 10000000. Why?
choices: The pattern is a special reserved value
The recipe only works for positive numbers
+128 is not representable in 8 bits, so the most negative value has no positive counterpart
An extra carry was discarded, which is a bug in the recipe
explanation: The range is -128 to 127, so there is no +128 for the negation to land on. This is real and it is in Java: Math.abs(Integer.MIN_VALUE) returns a negative number, by specification. Code that computes an absolute value and then assumes it is non-negative has a bug that fires once every four billion inputs.
